title: Tierra Blanca Joven eruption of Ilopango
summary: The Tierra Blanca Joven eruption of the Ilopango volcano in El Salvador is dated to 431 CE, give or take two years, from its ash layer in a Greenland ice core. A plume about 45 km high dispersed 37 to 82 cubic kilometres of magma and injected more sulfur than Pinatubo in 1991. Its major effects appear limited to people within about 80 km, whose land was buried in ash and left uninhabitable for years to decades.

uncertainty.note: The study gives 431 ± 2 CE; the start and end years here are 431 minus and plus 2. It conflicts with an older link to the 540s cold decade.

where.historical_name: Ilopango caldera, El Salvador, inhabited by the Maya at the time

importance.justification: Large eruption now dated precisely to 431 CE, with limited wider climate impact per the study.

beats.caption: The Tierra Blanca Joven eruption of Ilopango sends a plume about 45 km high into the sky.
Between 37 and 82 cubic kilometres of magma were dispersed by the plume.
Areas within about 80 km were covered in ash and became uninhabitable for years to decades.

reviewer_note: Least sure: nothing major. The caldera is 13 x 17 km per the study, so 15 km uncertainty on the Wikidata point. EurekAlert is a press release of the same study, so independence is publisher-level only. Link to the 536 record is a related link (the study disputes the old link to the 540s cold decade).
